standard.title: Share media arts in informal settings
standard.description: share media arts works with audiences in informal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share arts works informally and respond to audience questions. They have not yet shared specifically media arts works in ways that require permission, protocol consideration, or audience relationship thinking.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share media arts works with audiences in informal settings, applying permission principles and considering audience relationships.

nodes.label: Permission and protocols for sharing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and apply at least one permission consideration before sharing a media arts work.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one permission requirement before sharing a media work (e.g. asking peers before using their images) and apply it in a class sharing context.
nodes.typical_width: Apply permission principles across sharing contexts — obtaining individual permission for photographs, understanding that cultural material may belong to a group rather than an individual; consult relevant people or online safety resources; develop class rules for sharing.
wider: Develop a class set of rules for using and creating images, sounds and text in media arts works — presenting the rules to the class and explaining the reasoning behind each rule with a real scenario

Explore the difference between individual permission and permission for cultural material belonging to a collective group — using a specific scenario (e.g. a class news bulletin) to ground the distinction
nodes.hinge_reason: Permission principles are the non-negotiable precondition for any public sharing — without this, sharing activities cannot proceed ethically, and the habit is foundational to all future media arts practice.

response_modes.reason: Use real scenarios to build reasoning about permission — 'Before we share this photo of Jake, what do we need to do? Why?' Scenario-based reasoning transfers better than abstract rule recitation.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one permission requirement before sharing a media work
Student applies that permission principle in at least one class sharing activity

nodes.label: Presenting in informal settings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share a media arts work with an audience in an informal setting — presenting the work and explaining how it was made or what they enjoyed.
nodes.minimum_width: Present one media arts work to a class, small group or teacher — explain how it was made and at least one thing they enjoyed about making it.
nodes.typical_width: Present media arts works in informal settings (class, small group, another class); explain making process and enjoyment; collect and share class stories as a news bulletin; create and record a radio play for another class audience; document and seek permission for sharing.
wider: Collect and share class stories as a class news bulletin — applying permission protocols, acknowledging individual and cultural permissions, and presenting the bulletin in a live or recorded format

Create, rehearse and record a radio play in a small group — practising the full creation-to-sharing workflow, seeking permission to share with another class, and reflecting on what it felt like to have a real audience

Present a media arts work to a real community audience beyond the classroom (another class, assembly, school intranet) — considering how the larger audience changes how the work is prepared and presented

response_modes.reason: Vary the informal sharing contexts — small group, whole class, another class, recorded distribution — so students develop experience of different audience types and begin to understand how audience shapes presentation choices.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of informal sharing contexts at Y1-2 (class news bulletin, radio play for another class, school intranet, live class screening) is genuinely diverse — students who share across multiple contexts develop a much stronger sense of the maker-audience relationship.
success_criteria: Student presents a media arts work to an audience in an informal setting
Student explains how the work was made or what they enjoyed about making it
